markdown_report:
**Synthesis.** Three starting-point insights guide this early-stage search. (1) Embedding-conditioned retention may suppress stale state while preserving persistent preferences. This targets historical-interest carryover and insufficient priority for recent coherent behavior, but remains unverified. (2) Final-feature checks fail in all four categories despite zero aligned-valid-feature and candidate-score discrepancies. Isolate readout, transformations and numerical execution before changing the architecture; temporal effects remain unavailable. (3) Training negative-win rates span 0.68–4.29%. These sampled margins establish neither top-ten ranking quality nor validation generalization; embedding alignment scores of 0.505–0.5156 do not establish collapse.

Three literature insights suggest complementary directions. (1) GRU4Rec’s [BPR-max](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) emphasizes competitive negatives, motivating objective improvements. (2) [TedRec](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/TedRec) motivates joint text/ID representations, although its pretrained transformer evidence does not establish benefits for scratch-trained GRU text features. (3) [Interest-drift gates](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12674) and [GRU-D](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01865) motivate adaptive memory; GRU-D provides a closer hidden-state attenuation precedent. Neither validates this proposal on the pinned benchmark.

**Framework and candidates.** Organize interventions by target: execution correctness → memory selection → competitive ranking → item specificity. Correctness precedes mechanism interpretation. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Alignment scores describe hypotheses, not measured improvements.

| Atomic idea | Scores | Positive / negative assessment for each dimension |
|---|---|---|
| A. Embedding-conditioned retention before GRU updates | 4/6/8/5/5 | O: focused parameterization / established decay precedents; P: reusable memory control / uncertain gains; U: targets stale interests and weak recent priority / cannot establish compatibility; M: testable shared execution / retention does not repair readout; D: small cell change / throughput and parity work |
| B. Regularized BPR-max | 3/7/6/6/3 | O: principled transfer / established method; P: competitive ranking / hardness sensitivity; U: separates competitors / lacks intent labels; M: targets sampled-ranking weakness / cannot fix execution; D: compact loss / sampling care |
| C. Scratch-trained title/description encoder within GRU4Rec | 4/7/8/5/6 | O: constrained adaptation / familiar fusion; P: sparse-item sharing / limited supervision; U: identifiable content / compatibility may be absent; M: frequency-slice hypothesis / cannot fix execution; D: standard pooling / vocabulary and serving work |

**Selected: A, padding-invariant adaptive retention.** At 10% progress, retain the smallest architectural experiment after execution isolation. It targets two user failures: isolated historical interests dominating current needs and recent repeated behavior receiving insufficient priority. The shared readout addresses the measured execution inconsistency; the gate itself has no demonstrated diagnostic benefit.

For each layer, compute `g=sigmoid(A*e+B*h+b)` and `h_new=GRUCell(x,g*h)`, supplying the observed ID embedding `e` directly to every gate. This attenuates all recurrent pathways, including direct carry. Initialize weights to zero and `b=logit(0.999)`; the earlier bias-four proposal gives retention 0.982 and appreciable cumulative attenuation. No finite sigmoid bias exactly recovers baseline behavior.

Compare corrected baseline, weight-copied custom-cell control with `g=1`, and learned gating as separate trials. Preserve dropout, objective and optimizer. Freeze padding states and gather the greatest nonpadding index; empty features are zero. Share training, ModelView and predictor code. Retain diagnostic interfaces, stagewise execution checks and gate summaries; run temporal probes only after checks pass. Preserve routing, seeds, limits and one checkpoint per category. Select exclusively by official macro validation HR@10, accounting for GPU cost; no gain is established.

idea.description: Add a coordinate-wise, ID-embedding-conditioned retention gate before each ordinary GRU4Rec recurrent update. Establish execution consistency separately through explicit padding semantics, a shared feature/readout/scoring implementation, and an identity-gate implementation control.
idea.motivation: Test whether adaptive memory reduces isolated historical influence and prioritizes recent coherent behavior. These address two reported user-facing failures, while exact compatibility, satisfied purchase needs and mood remain unobserved. Resolve measured final-feature execution failures before interpreting temporal diagnostics. Strong sampled training separation does not establish validation quality.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected GRU4Rec family and baseline loss, optimizer, negative sampling, valid-target masking, loss reduction, initialization and embedding/interlayer/output dropout for the architectural comparison. First isolate execution failures on the unchanged baseline: capture one sequence-feature tensor and compare its production readout with an independent maximum-nonzero-index gather from that same tensor. Assert indices exactly for empty, singleton, mixed-length and full-length rows. Distinguish raw recurrent outputs from transformed recommendation features. Compare actual model, ModelView and embedded predictor at each stage. Then separately compare individual versus batched execution and additional leading padding. Use model.eval() and inference mode; functional dropout must specify training=self.training. Preserve existing tolerances and report unresolved discrepancies. Controlled float64/backend reruns can investigate numerical effects; they must not silently change checkpoint semantics or conceal failures.

Use g_t^l=sigmoid(A^l e_t+B^l h_previous^l+b^l), with the observed item ID embedding supplied directly to every layer's gate. Upper-layer GRU inputs still come from the preceding layer. Passing g*h as the GRUCell hidden argument changes reset, update, candidate and direct-carry computations; it is not merely another candidate reset gate. Preserve the actual baseline's PyTorch GRU algebra. Initialize A and B to zero and the total gate bias to logit(0.999), approximately 6.9068. The original bias-four initialization remains a documented alternative rather than the default: sigmoid(4) is approximately 0.982, whose direct-path retention factor over 100 steps is approximately 0.163. Even 0.999 gives approximately 0.905 over 100 steps, before ordinary GRU effects; these factors are not complete hidden-state Jacobians. No finite sigmoid initialization exactly recovers baseline behavior.

Compare three separate configurations: corrected baseline; custom-cell control with gate bypassed exactly at one; learned gating. Copy corresponding baseline embedding, recurrent, readout and scoring weights into the identity implementation for evaluation-mode parity checks before training. Preserve baseline training initialization and randomization procedures across experimental configurations; identical seed values do not guarantee identical random draws after adding parameters. Preserve dropout locations, probabilities and mask semantics rather than assuming a timestep loop reproduces fused GRU dropout. Each trial trains one independent network per category; controls are never combined at inference. Optional removal of direct embedding conditioning is a later separately budgeted ablation, not part of the initial experiment.

Freeze every recurrent layer's state on padding, mask padded output features, and gather the greatest nonzero position rather than count-1. Empty histories yield zero features while retaining any learned scoring bias. Maintain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and the actual module's score_candidates, including BxLxK scoring. Use one architecture definition for training and the predictor writer; serialize architecture dimensions, dropout settings, gate configuration and state_dict together. Save one selected checkpoint per category without score fusion, averaging or separately fitted popularity/transition components.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and their definitions. Preserve the actual trained module in view.model and all ModelView compatibility interfaces. After execution checks pass, rerun the existing temporal probe without changing its population, candidates, interventions or uncertainty definitions. In evaluation mode, additionally measure gate means, quantiles, fractions below 0.05/above 0.95 and ||g*h||/||h|| for nonzero previous-state norms, by layer and history-length bin, excluding padding and reporting denominators. Gate saturation does not establish useful forgetting. Inspect training-frequency margin slices; do not interpret embedding alignment near 0.5 as recommendation diversity or evidence of collapse.

Measure synchronized forward/backward step time, examples per second and peak GPU memory on representative batches. Report matched-update comparisons alongside GPU-seconds because GRUCell loops can lose fused-sequence throughput. All controls, diagnostics and failures consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], artifacts beneath the trial directory, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, supplied splits and fixed evaluator. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing. Select configurations exclusively through official four-category macro validation HR@10; report category validation results as context. Fix the experiment list before comparing results and avoid an extensive gate-initialization sweep, since repeated validation selection can overfit 200 validation users per category. No test labels, other-trial checkpoints, pretrained weights or unavailable metadata are used.

The gate can learn item-frequency shortcuts, suppress useful older preferences or memorize training transitions. Compare validation performance with the identity control and training-frequency diagnostics; training margins and gate summaries cannot establish reduced shortcut learning. Titles/descriptions may support a later jointly trained text experiment, but this selected gate uses only learned IDs and previous states. Broad association, compatibility, redundancy and experiential fit remain hypotheses rather than observed intent labels.
idea.pseudocode:
# Specification: integrate into the supplied baseline while preserving its dropout and scoring semantics.
class RetentionGRULayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, embedding_dim, input_dim, hidden_dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.gate_e = nn.Linear(embedding_dim, hidden_dim, bias=True)
        self.gate_h = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim, bias=False)
        self.gru_cell = nn.GRUCell(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.gate_e.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.gate_h.weight)
        nn.init.constant_(self.gate_e.bias, math.log(0.999 / 0.001))

    def step(self, e, x, h, valid, identity_control=False):
        gate = torch.ones_like(h) if identity_control else torch.sigmoid(
            self.gate_e(e) + self.gate_h(h))
        proposal = self.gru_cell(x, gate * h)
        return torch.where(valid[:, None], proposal, h)

# Initialize every recurrent state to zero.
# Preserve the baseline's embedding/interlayer/output dropout exactly.
for t in range(sequence.shape[1]):
    valid = sequence[:, t].ne(0)
    e = item_emb(sequence[:, t])
    x = baseline_embedding_dropout(e)
    for layer_index, layer in enumerate(layers):
        states[layer_index] = layer.step(
            e, x, states[layer_index], valid, identity_control)
        x = states[layer_index]
        if layer_index < len(layers) - 1:
            x = baseline_interlayer_dropout(x, layer_index, t)
    x = baseline_output_transform(x)
    features[:, t] = torch.where(valid[:, None], x, torch.zeros_like(x))

# Shared production readout; handle zero-width inputs explicitly if supported.
B, L = sequence.shape
positions = torch.arange(L, device=sequence.device)
idx = torch.where(sequence.ne(0), positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
final = features.gather(
    1, idx.clamp_min(0)[:, None, None].expand(-1, 1, features.shape[-1])
).squeeze(1)
final = torch.where(idx[:, None].ge(0), final, torch.zeros_like(final))
# Use the same scoring function, including learned biases, everywhere.

# Before architecture experiments:
# 1. Capture baseline features once; compare production and independent readouts.
# 2. Assert readout indices and empty-history behavior exactly.
# 3. Separately test padding, batch-shape and predictor agreement at fixed tolerances.
# 4. Copy baseline weights into the gate=1 control and verify eval-mode parity.
# 5. Train the prespecified independent configurations with fixed baseline settings.
# 6. Measure throughput, execution consistency, gate summaries and available diagnostics.
# 7. Select by official macro validation HR@10; deploy one checkpoint per category.

originality.positive: The explicit embedding-conditioned pre-update parameterization is a focused, falsifiable GRU4Rec extension with clear single-network implementation.
originality.negative: Hidden-state decay and context-dependent recurrent gating have substantial precedent, including GRU-D; novelty is incremental rather than a new memory-model class.

future_potential.positive: Controlled evidence could support further study of selective memory and distinguish adaptive retention from ordinary GRU behavior.
future_potential.negative: Temporal evidence is currently unavailable, validation gains are unreported, and additional attenuation may harm persistent preferences.

code_difficulty.positive: The gate requires few parameters and no extra datasets, pretrained components or independent predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful fused-GRU replacement requires dropout and algebra parity, checkpoint/predictor integration, execution isolation and throughput measurement.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces ranking objectives including BPR-max that emphasize high-scoring negative competitors.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the proposed retention gate or the pinned four-category evaluation.
Hard-negative weighting does not identify false negatives or supply intent labels.

related_work.title: TedRec
contributions: Studies integration of text and collaborative item representations through sequence-level fusion.
limitations: Its pretrained text features and SASRec backbone do not directly validate scratch-trained text features within GRU4Rec.
Text availability does not guarantee equipment compatibility or current-purpose annotations.

related_work.title: Hierarchical recurrent recommendation with interest-drift gates
contributions: Provides related precedent for explicitly modeling changing interests with recurrent gates.
limitations: Does not establish the effectiveness of the proposed embedding-conditioned pre-update retention gate on this benchmark.

related_work.title: GRU-D: Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values
contributions: Provides a closer placement precedent by decaying hidden state before recurrent processing.
limitations: Addresses a different domain and missingness mechanism.
Does not validate the proposed ID-embedding-conditioned recommendation gate.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Defines recurrent equations, hidden-state layout and interlayer dropout placement.
Explains why zero-valued padding inputs alone do not guarantee unchanged state.
limitations: Documents execution semantics rather than recommendation accuracy or the cause of the reported discrepancies.
Equivalent mathematical operations can still differ numerically across execution paths.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRUCell documentation
contributions: Specifies the cell algebra needed for an identity-gate implementation control.
Shows that substituting a gated hidden argument also changes direct old-state carry.
limitations: A timestep loop does not automatically reproduce fused-GRU dropout behavior or throughput.

related_work.title: PyTorch gather documentation
contributions: Defines indexed tensor gathering used for an independent same-pass final-position readout.
limitations: Correct gathering still requires correct nonpadding indices and explicit empty-history handling.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy notes
contributions: Explains numerical differences across batching shapes and execution implementations.
Motivates separating same-pass readout checks from cross-execution comparisons.
limitations: Does not establish that the observed failures are harmless or authorize relaxing benchmark diagnostic tolerances.

related_work.title: PyTorch functional dropout documentation
contributions: Documents the training argument required to disable functional dropout during evaluation.
limitations: Correct evaluation-mode dropout does not establish complete architectural or numerical parity.
